milestones.title: The first arrival
milestones.text: The inaugural rally leaves Paris in December 1978 and reaches Dakar in January 1979. Cyril Neveu and Alain Génestier head the bike and car results.

milestones.title: All the way to Cape Town
milestones.text: The finish moves to South Africa. Hubert Auriol wins in cars, adding to his earlier motorcycle victories.

milestones.title: Kleinschmidt makes history
milestones.text: Jutta Kleinschmidt becomes the first woman to win the Dakar car category, driving a Mitsubishi.

milestones.title: A year without a start
milestones.text: The scheduled Lisbon–Dakar is cancelled before departure over security concerns. It has no results and contributes nothing to the statistics.

milestones.title: A different continent
milestones.text: The rally begins its South American era. South Africa’s Giniel de Villiers wins in cars for Volkswagen.

milestones.title: Saudi Arabia
milestones.text: The rally enters its third geographical era. Ricky Brabec wins on a Honda, ending KTM’s run of 18 consecutive held bike editions.

method: Every edition in Wikipedia’s Dakar Rally article, read at the recorded revision: its route as the article names it (start, waypoint, finish), its era, and the first three of every category as the article lists them — the lead driver or rider and the crew, and the make. The map draws each route schematically between its named towns over the Natural Earth land silhouette; the stage-by-stage course is not carried. The 2008 edition, cancelled before the start, has no results and counts nothing. Beyond the podium, the final classification is carried wherever a rally-year article under the same licence prints it — positions 4–10 for 1985, 1990, 1995, 2000, 2010 and 2015, and what the 2022–2026 articles give, up to the whole classification — with the entry lists the 2022, 2023 and 2025 articles print. No non-finisher is carried: no licensed source lists them.

classification.rightsPolicy: Included data only where the source states a clear redistribution license. Unlicensed or unclear sources were not copied into the records.
classification.scope: Complete rights-cleared consolidation of the existing podium-only atlas plus previous licensed structured harvests. Includes all 534 podium rows from 1979–2026 and 1,133 non-podium classifications from licensed Wikipedia sources, plus captured 2022–2025 entrant-roster rows. Classifications cover source years 1985, 1990, 1995, 2000, 2010, 2015, 2022–2026; the podium atlas covers years/categories as enumerated in podiumSource.
limitations: Recent Wikipedia tables vary by category and year and frequently stop at position 10.
No non-finisher records are included because the sources located for these entries did not have clear redistribution rights.
The 2025 roster is the set of rows captured from the licensed article, not a claim of a complete official entrant register.
The 2026 article and its results are subject to change after publication.
The consolidated harvest does not include earlier factory/team findings, official non-finisher records, or records from sources where clear redistribution rights were not verified.
Non-podium coverage is available only for the specific years/categories represented in the source tables; it is not a complete historical finisher register.
